ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 3 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — John Locke

code.originalText: Twelve-week asthma review with repeat spirometry after pulmonary rehabilitation

text.paragraph: Twelve-week asthma review with repeat spirometry. [S]

Mr. Locke returns twelve weeks after starting budesonide-formoterol as maintenance and reliever. He finished the eight-week pulmonary rehabilitation program, attending all 16 sessions, and walks 30 minutes five days a week. He needs three or four extra inhalations a week, mostly after his days in the city, and woke at night with cough once in the past month. He has had no flare and no oral corticosteroids. The dose counter matches his diary, with about one missed evening dose a fortnight. He has had no hoarseness or sore mouth. His home peak flow is best at 440 L/min in the mornings and falls to about 360 after a city day. The open fires stay out; a small air monitor in his study usually reads below 10 ug/m3 of PM2.5. He has spent two or three days a month in the city and stayed away during an air quality alert in May. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-06-18; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Good air entry; a few end-expiratory wheezes on forced expiration; oxygen saturation 97 percent

Chronic cough with wheeze and breathlessness since his late thirties, worse every winter and within a day of any stay in the city or by an open fire, better in warm weather and country air; night cough two or three times a week this winter; under evaluation
S — Synthetic presenting problem echoing his documented lifelong cough and breathlessness in London's coal smoke; superseded by the diagnosis at the second visit.
Long exposure to urban air pollution (decades in a large city with heavy traffic and coal and wood burning) and to indoor solid-fuel smoke from open coal and wood fires at home
S — Synthetic modern exposure echoing the coal smoke that he, Sydenham, and Lady Masham blamed for his cough; no historical level of exposure is asserted.

Asthma with persistent airflow limitation, type 2 (eosinophilic) phenotype, in a never-smoker: post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC 0.62, FEV1 62 percent predicted rising 380 mL after albuterol, FeNO 41 ppb, eosinophils 0.46 x 10^3/uL, IgE 186 IU/mL, normal DLCO, no emphysema on CT; aggravated by air pollution and indoor smoke; not COPD
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis. His lifelong cough and breathlessness worse in coal smoke are documented (D); calling them asthma is a modern retrospective reading (R).

list.item:
Asthma with persistent airflow limitation, type 2 phenotype (J45.40). Much better but not yet well controlled: Asthma Control Test 19 and reliever use three or four times a week, with no flares. FEV1 2.46 L before bronchodilator (73 percent predicted), up 350 mL, and 2.58 L after, with a post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC of 0.63, still below the lower limit of normal: a large improvement, but airflow limitation persists. FeNO has fallen from 41 to 22 ppb, showing that he is taking the inhaled corticosteroid and that his type 2 inflammation has responded. Adherence and technique are good. The six-minute walk improved by 75 m after rehabilitation. Because residual symptoms come with persistent airflow limitation and low FeNO, adding tiotropium (GINA step 5 add-on LAMA) is preferred over a higher corticosteroid dose; a biologic is not indicated. [S]
Add tiotropium 2.5 mcg soft-mist inhaler, two inhalations once daily; technique taught today.
Continue budesonide-formoterol two inhalations twice daily plus one as needed, no more than 12 a day.
Action plan updated with peak-flow zones from his best of 440 L/min: green 352 or more, yellow 220 to 351, red below 220.
Keep up the walking program.
Review at his preventive visit in three months and with an Asthma Control Test at four months.

Exposure to air pollution and indoor solid-fuel smoke (Z77.110). Indoor smoke removed; outdoor exposure reduced by planning around alerts. City days still bring symptoms. [S]
Continue the exposure plan; keep city visits to days with an air quality index below 100.
